categories.name: Rapid Triage / Outpatient Workup
categories.description: Short, fast-paced pathways ending quickly with basic triage or initial blood work (CRP/Leucocytes) without admission, typically completing within minutes.
categories.rationale: Grounded in short trace lengths, low durations, and early terminal activities like ER Sepsis Triage, CRP, or Leucocytes.

categories.name: Acute IV Intervention
categories.description: Mid-length pathways featuring administration of intravenous fluids and antibiotics alongside standard blood panels, resolving within hours.
categories.rationale: Characterized by the inclusion of IV Liquid and IV Antibiotics and intermediate durations (1-4 hours).

categories.name: Standard Inpatient Admission & Release
categories.description: Pathways requiring ward admission (Admission NC/IC) followed by multi-day observation and eventual successful release (Release A, B, C, or D).
categories.rationale: Reflects standard hospital stays involving nursing or intensive care admissions and structured release outcomes.

categories.name: Readmission / Extended Complication Path
categories.description: Complex, highly repetitive or long-duration pathways that result in patient readmissions or return to the emergency room ('Return ER').
categories.rationale: Identified by exceptionally long durations (weeks to over a year), high trace lengths, and the 'Return ER' final outcome.
